h1: Baan Suan La Moon — a house in a fruit garden that feels like staying with a friend in the heart of Chiang Khan
intro: If you want to stay in Chiang Khan somewhere quiet and private but still walk to the walking street and the Mekong — Baan Suan La Moon is a tiny 6-room guesthouse set in a fruit garden that many travellers say feels more like staying at a relative's house than a hotel · The two things reviews mention again and again are the kind, attentive owner and the leafy garden that makes the place feel restful · From approx. ฿750/night

body.html: Baan Suan La Moon is a little house in a garden, not a hotel block on the walking street · It sits down a quiet lane about 300 m off the main road in Chiang Khan Subdistrict, Chiang Khan District · With only 6 rooms set among fruit trees, the feel is homestay-friendly, and the thing guests mention most is the kind owner, who happily recommends places to eat and explore and looks after guests like family.

The rooms are warm-toned garden bungalows, with options for couples and for families · Every room has air conditioning, a fridge and toiletries · The décor is simple and clean rather than luxurious, but many guests praise how clean and comfortable they are, which makes this a budget Chiang Khan stay that doesn't feel cramped · The rooms look out onto the garden, so you wake up to greenery rather than a wall.
"It felt like staying at a relative's house — the owner was so kind, the garden quiet and shady, and it's an easy walk to the walking street and the river."

The main charm here is the shady fruit garden · There are sitting spots under the trees, and at times the owner will happily let you pick fruit from the garden · The quiet is something guests rate highly, because even though Chiang Khan gets busy, the property is tucked down a lane, so it's far quieter than the stays right on the walking street · It suits anyone who wants calm at night after a day of wandering the market.

The location strikes a nice balance of quiet and convenience · It's about a 10–15 minute walk to Chiang Khan Walking Street and the Mekong River, roughly 500 m to the riverbank · In the morning you can step out to join the sticky-rice alms-giving, a Chiang Khan highlight · The guesthouse lends bicycles free of charge — many guests ride along the river at dawn or dusk — and there's free parking for those who drive.

A few things to understand before you book · This is a small guesthouse, not a full resort — there's no pool, no lift, and breakfast is a simple affair, with the owner sometimes laying on a local breakfast and sometimes none at all, so ask ahead if you need it · A few items, such as a hair dryer, are borrowed from the owner rather than provided in every room · If you want full hotel facilities, weigh that up here.

Plainly put, Baan Suan La Moon isn't for travellers who want a Mekong view from the room or a full set of facilities · But if what you're after is a quiet garden house, an owner who looks after you, budget pricing and a location you can walk from to the walking street and the river — this delivers more than its price suggests · A score of around 9.1 and steady praise for the owner and the cleanliness show plenty of guests are happy to trade luxury for warmth and quiet.

A tip from following the reviews: with only 6 rooms, it fills fast in the cool season, so book ahead, especially on long weekends · Message the owner in advance about breakfast and pick-up, and if you're travelling as a family, ask for a room that sleeps several · Borrow a bicycle and ride along the Mekong at first light while the mist still lingers — it's when Chiang Khan looks its best.

faqTitle: Frequently asked questions — Baan Suan La Moon

faq.q: Where is Baan Suan La Moon and is it near Chiang Khan Walking Street?
faq.a: The guesthouse is at 91/11 Moo 1, Soi 5 Bon, Chiang Khan Subdistrict, Chiang Khan District, Loei Province · It's down a quiet lane about 300 m off the main road · It's roughly a 10–15 minute walk to Chiang Khan Walking Street and the Mekong (about 500 m to the riverbank), and it sits near the morning sticky-rice alms-giving route.

faq.q: What are the starting prices and room types at Baan Suan La Moon?
faq.a: Prices start at approximately ฿750/night for a garden-view double · The family (Quadruple) room with two queen beds is around ฿1,300 · There are 6 rooms in total, all with air conditioning and a fridge · Prices depend on dates and holidays, so compare a few platforms before booking.

faq.q: Who is Baan Suan La Moon best for?
faq.a: It's best for travellers who want a quiet garden stay in Chiang Khan, at a budget price, with a caring owner, while still being able to walk to the walking street and the river · It suits couples, small families, or anyone who likes a homestay feel · It's not for those who want a river view from the room or full resort facilities.

faq.q: Is there breakfast, and are bicycles available?
faq.a: Breakfast is a simple affair — the owner sometimes lays on a local breakfast and sometimes none at all, so ask ahead if you need it · The guesthouse lends bicycles free of charge, with many guests riding along the Mekong at dawn or dusk, and there's free parking for those who drive.

faq.q: Is it quiet, and is there a pool or a lift?
faq.a: Because it's tucked down a lane in a garden, it's far quieter than stays right on the walking street, which suits anyone wanting calm at night · It's a small guesthouse with no pool and no lift, and a few items such as a hair dryer are borrowed from the owner.

faq.q: How far ahead should I book?
faq.a: With only 6 rooms, it fills fast in the cool season (November–January) and on long weekends, so book several weeks ahead · Every platform offers a Free Cancellation option — pick that if your plans aren't firm — and message the owner to confirm breakfast and pick-up in advance.
